stableDprAutoFollowUp.method: Physical iPhone, stable-DPR build before immediate reflection-bake cleanup; scripted normal Auto rotate button.

observations: Native manual-window frame durations remain below 33.333 ms for all 600 recorded frames; these are browser rendering frames, not GPU execution or display presentation measurements.

The initial activation includes an approximately 1.332-second native frame, with approximately 1.28 seconds attributed to script in the inspector. This cold-start cost is separate from the settled interaction window.

The pinned renderer emits a THREE.Clock deprecation warning per mount. A later extended textured reopen run also reaches Safari context-quota warnings and INVALID_OPERATION: loseContext: context already lost. Lost/detached counters alone do not prove native context capacity is reclaimed.
Graphics context loss and stable live counts do not establish a phone CPU/OS/GPU memory trend.

afterStop.note: The one-second wait did not exclude all damping; the longer post-stop sequence confirms eventual idle.

afterLongerSettle.note: A residual frame occurred in this short window; the longer post-stop sequence confirms eventual idle.

postStopSequence.note: Damping draws cease within the first four seconds; the final six seconds contain no model draws.

bitmapLifetimeAfterRepeat.method: Test-only wrapper around native createImageBitmap and each returned bitmap.close, installed before activation. Counters retain no bitmap objects or model data.

nativeMemory.method: Native Safari Memory timeline with Collect garbage requested through Inspector before and after another ten reopens; model closed at both ends. Memory instrumentation configured without screenshots. Raw export remains ignored and owner-readable.
nativeMemory.result: Inconclusive native-memory trend: JavaScript category decreases, but Page and total categories increase. Do not claim the phone memory acceptance check passed; distinguish allocator/browser capacity from retained application objects with a longer plateau/allocation study.
nativeMemory.contextQuotaWarnings: During the second textured reopen batch, Safari reports too many active WebGL contexts and already-lost context errors despite previous contexts being recorded as lost/detached. Cause not isolated; no native-memory pass.

followUpAnalysis.method: Reanalyze the already captured numeric Safari Memory samples; no new device measurement.
followUpAnalysis.interpretation: The final idle window levels off slightly downward; it does not prove earlier Page growth was reclaimed or establish long-term retention.

relatedBrowserReport.finding: WebKit reports the same too-many-contexts/already-lost warnings in a plain WebGL reproduction; a 2026 comment reports continued reproduction on iOS 26.3. Supporting evidence only, not proof that all observed native-memory growth is browser-owned.

realVisibilityChecks.note: Multiple real hidden/visible events observed; one boundary records one additional submitted frame. This is separate from simulated browser coverage.

subjectiveFeedback.question: Did any of the three models stutter? Is the iPhone charging, is Low Power Mode on or off, and does it feel noticeably warm?
subjectiveFeedback.interpretation: Initial feedback reports no perceived stuttering. Superseded for overall visual correctness by the later landscape clipping and flicker report. Charging, Low Power Mode and thermal state were not separately confirmed.

reportedRegressions.userReport: in sideway full screen the model isn't centred. also, after I move it for a while and stop, the model starts flickering fir a few minutes and then stops flickering
reportedRegressions.screenshot: IMG_0622.PNG supplied by user; textured model visibly clipped at the lower edge of the landscape stage
reportedRegressions.expandedMode: Dialog fallback; device events show fullscreen false, dialog true
reportedRegressions.response: Bind the Canvas wrapper to the actual clamped stage using absolute positioning; keep DPR stable during orbit instead of changing it between motion and rest. User confirms the subsequent physical iPhone retest works.

physicalRetest.requestedChecks: Textured model in landscape expanded preview; move the model and stop, checking centering and whether flicker returns.
physicalRetest.result: User-confirmed visual pass for the two reported defects.
physicalRetest.build: Fresh isolated production session with the absolute Canvas layout, top-aligned expanded dialog and stable DPR.
physicalRetest.limits: Subjective confirmation only; no new frame, memory, thermal or timing measurements were supplied. Does not resolve the earlier extended-session memory/context-quota observations.

androidDecision.userInstruction: continue with 9.3 and let's asume that if it works in ios it will work in android
androidDecision.status: Physical testing waived by project owner; compatibility assumed, unverified.

plainWebglControl.device: Same physical iPhone 15, Safari remote inspector
plainWebglControl.method: Create 24 unattached canvas WebGL2 contexts, request WEBGL_lose_context on each, yield 50 ms between contexts. No GemuKore Canvas or diagnostic probe active. Request native Inspector Collect garbage afterward. Keep only WeakRefs to contexts.
observedWarnings: There are too many active WebGL contexts on this page, the oldest context will be lost.
WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: loseContext: context already lost
plainWebglControl.interpretation: The warning pair reproduces independently of GemuKore viewer/loader/probe and all control contexts become unreachable after requested GC. This supports the documented WebKit context-accounting limitation; it does not by itself establish application memory behavior.

stableDprFollowUp.software: Stable DPR and corrected landscape Canvas layout; before immediate reflection-bake cleanup optimization.
stableDprFollowUp.method: Two batches of ten scripted open/close sessions on the actual iPhone; native Memory timeline active; garbage collection requested at batch boundaries. WeakRefs retained only for diagnostics.

nativeMemory.result: Native Page/total grows during the batch and settles downward afterward. Application graphics disposal is observed, but native retention remains an explicit Safari limitation/inconclusive check, not a native-memory pass.

viewerWithoutProbe.method: Fresh page, no graphics probe or bitmap wrapper. Twenty scripted normal viewer sessions, followed by another twenty. Native context-loss listeners and WeakRefs only.
viewerWithoutProbe.diagnosticExperiments: Clearing console history, reconnecting Inspector and zeroing already-detached canvases did not eliminate the wrapper retention. No such workaround was added to application code.

nativeMemory.result: Native Page/total grows during the batch and settles downward afterward. Application graphics disposal is observed, but native retention remains an explicit Safari limitation/inconclusive check, not a native-memory pass.

liveReducedMotionFollowUp.method: Safari Inspector page-scoped Reduce motion override on the physical iPhone; this is not a change to the iOS system preference.

loadingCancelFollowUp.method: Real private fetch on the iPhone, with a test-only Response stream delivering buffered 64-byte chunks every 250 ms. This is controlled client delivery, not a physical-network throughput benchmark. Original fetch restored before retry.
loadingCancelFollowUp.harnessNote: First attempt queried View in 3D before React committed the preceding Close. Repeated with UI settling; successful result recorded. The setup error is not an application failure.

followUps: Native Safari retention remains inconclusive despite observed resource disposal and reproduction of context-quota warnings in plain WebGL; do not claim a native-memory pass.
Power/Low Power Mode/thermal conditions unspecified; no thermal or full-budget device guarantee.
Final immediate reflection-bake resource cleanup is verified separately by software regression tests; physical numbers above precede that final optimization.

finalCleanupSoftwareVerification.scope: Immediate reflection-bake cleanup, including the pinned room InstancedMesh buffers; baked reflection remains until close. Physical measurements above precede this final optimization.
finalCleanupSoftwareVerification.environment: Production Chromium/SwiftShader, desktop and mobile viewport emulation; not a phone measurement.
